# 04 — Image Prompt Guidelines

**No images are generated by this blueprint.** Every image location in `pages/` contains a labelled placeholder with a production-ready prompt. This document defines the house art direction those prompts all inherit, so the whole library reads as one commissioned shoot rather than a folder of AI outputs.

---

## 1. Placeholder format

Every image location in `pages/` uses exactly this block. Do not vary it.

```
### IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — <ID>

**Purpose:** <what this image has to do for the page, in one sentence>
**Aspect ratio:** <ratio> · **Display size:** <max rendered px> · **Loading:** <lazy | eager>
**Save to:** src/assets/<page>/<name>.{avif,webp}
**Suggested composition:** <framing, subject placement, where the negative space sits, what the eye does>
**Alt text:** <the actual alt attribute to ship, or `""` if decorative>

**Higgsfield prompt:**
```
<command>
```
```

IDs are prefixed by page group: `H-` home · `P-` product · `S-` science · `O-` our story · `W-` wellbeing · `F-` FAQ · `B-` buy · `J-` journal · `C-` company.

---

## 2. House art direction

Every prompt inherits this. It is repeated in each prompt's wording — not abbreviated to a reference — because image models do not carry context between jobs.

**The shoot, described as if briefing a photographer:**

> One photographer, one trip, one set of lenses. Natural light only — early morning or the last hour before dusk, never midday. Warm daylight falling across deep green shadow. Everything sits still; nothing is staged mid-action for the camera. Materials are real and worn: rough sandstone, unfinished oak, dry steppe grass, linen, hand-thrown ceramic, cool steel, dusty leather. Colour is restrained and slightly desaturated, anchored to deep forest green, warm ivory and a single note of aged gold. There is grain, because it was shot on film. There are imperfections — a fingerprint on glass, dust in a light shaft, an uneven fold of cloth — because a perfect surface reads as rendered.

**Every prompt must contain, in its own words:**

| Requirement | How it appears in the prompt |
|---|---|
| Photorealistic | "editorial photograph", "documentary photograph", "still life photograph" — never "render", "illustration", "3D" |
| Natural lighting | Name the source: "low morning sun through a window", "raking golden side light", "overcast north light" |
| Real materials and texture | Name at least two: sandstone, oak, linen, steel, ceramic, grass, leather, wool |
| Subtle imperfection | "subtle film grain" plus one specific flaw: dust motes, a fingerprint, a worn edge, an uneven weave |
| Restrained colour | "palette of deep forest green, warm cream and aged gold", "desaturated", "muted" |
| Negative space | State *where*: "upper third left clean for a headline", "generous empty space along the right edge" |
| Mongolian heritage (where applicable) | Concrete and specific — a wooden churn, a ger door frame, steppe grass, a milking pail, tack and rope |

**Every prompt must avoid** (state these as negatives where the model supports it, and simply never describe them otherwise):

CGI · 3D render · digital art · illustration · HDR · oversaturated colour · plastic or waxy skin · perfect symmetry · lens flare · bokeh balls · stock-photo smiling · white seamless studio background · floating product with glowing halo · scattered ingredients arranged in an arc · water splash frozen mid-air · blue-and-white "clinical supplement" styling · text, logos, watermarks or graphic overlays baked into the image.

That last bullet is critical: **no typography in any generated image.** All text is HTML, always.

---

## 3. Two pipelines

Follows the convention already established in `STEPPE_GUT_HIGGSFIELD_PROMPTS.md`.

### 3.1 Product imagery — `product-photoshoot`

Use whenever a Steppe Gut pack, sachet, capsule bottle or pouch is in frame.

```
higgsfield product-photoshoot create --mode <product_shot|lifestyle_scene|conceptual_product> \
  --prompt "<short intent brief — the backend enhancer writes the full photographic prompt>" \
  --image <path to the supplied pack cutout> --aspect_ratio <ratio>
```

- `--prompt` is a **short intent brief**, not a full photographic prompt. The backend owns assembly. Over-writing it makes results worse.
- `--image` passes the real pack cutout so label and pack geometry are preserved. **Always supply it where a real asset exists** — this is what "preserve the supplied Steppe Gut bottle exactly" means in practice.
- `product_shot` mode rejects `4:5`. Use `3:4` and crop to 4:5 in CSS.
- There is no `--resolution` flag on this pipeline.

**Available reference cutouts** (existing in the repo — reuse, never regenerate):

| Asset | Path |
|---|---|
| Sachet box | `src/hero-product-box.png` |
| Loose sachets | `src/sachets-cutout.png` |
| Capsule jar | `src/assets/home/product-capsules.*` (produced in the earlier home pass) |

### 3.2 Story, place and science imagery — `generate create`

Use when no product is in frame: steppe, herders, fermentation vessels, macro texture, hands, interiors.

```
higgsfield generate create gpt_image_2 \
  --prompt "<full photographic prompt — you own every word>" \
  --aspect_ratio <ratio> --resolution 2k --wait
```

---

## 4. Prompt anatomy

Every `generate create` prompt is written in this order. Consistent ordering is what makes the set cohere.

1. **Shot type and subject** — "close editorial photograph of…", "cinematic wide photograph of…"
2. **The specific thing, with material detail** — "a worn oak fermentation churn bound in leather, mare's milk at the rim"
3. **Setting** — "inside a dim ger, the felt wall behind it"
4. **Light, named and directional** — "a single shaft of warm amber light falling from the roof ring"
5. **What the light does** — "raking across the milk surface, leaving the far side in deep green shadow"
6. **Negative space instruction** — "the upper left third of the frame kept calm and empty for a headline"
7. **Palette** — "palette of deep forest green, warm cream and aged gold, desaturated"
8. **Texture and imperfection** — "documentary texture, dust in the light, subtle film grain"

**A worked example:**

```
higgsfield generate create gpt_image_2 \
  --prompt "close editorial photograph of a worn oak fermentation churn bound with dark leather straps, fresh mare's milk resting at the rim with a faint skin on its surface, standing on a packed earth floor inside a dim Mongolian ger, a single shaft of warm amber light falling from the roof ring and raking across the milk while the far side of the vessel stays in deep green shadow, the upper left third of the frame calm and empty for a headline, palette of deep forest green warm cream and aged gold, desaturated, documentary texture with dust visible in the light shaft, subtle film grain, no text or graphic overlays" \
  --aspect_ratio 3:2 --resolution 2k --wait
```

---

## 5. Negative space by slot type

The single most common failure is a beautiful image that cannot hold the text it was made for. Specify the empty region explicitly, every time.

| Slot | Text position | Required empty region |
|---|---|---|
| Full-bleed chapter hero | Lower left | Bottom-left 40% low-detail and tonally dark, so cream text sits on it |
| Home hero | Left half | Left 45% quiet; subject weighted right of centre |
| Media/text row | Text is beside, not on, the image | No constraint — compose freely, but keep the subject off the inner edge so it isn't cropped when the row stacks |
| Card image | Caption sits below | Subject centred, ~12% breathing room on all sides for the 4:5 crop |
| Closing CTA bookend | Centred, upper third | Top third open sky or plain surface |
| Product hero | Right-hand buy card overlaps | Right 40% clean; product weighted left |

---

## 6. Consistency devices

Six recurring elements bind the library together. Reuse them; do not invent new ones per page.

| Device | Description |
|---|---|
| **The stone** | A rough, pale sandstone surface or plinth. Appears in every product still life |
| **The green ground** | Deep forest-green backdrop, fabric or painted wall, in every studio-type shot |
| **The gold hour** | Low warm sun from one side, never front-on, never overhead |
| **The grass** | Wind-brushed steppe grass, in every outdoor frame |
| **The vessel** | Worn oak and leather fermentation churn — the brand's recurring object |
| **The hand** | Where a person appears, they are shown working — pouring, binding, milking — rarely posed and never smiling at camera |

---

## 7. People in images

- **No faces to camera.** Hands, backs, three-quarter turns, figures at distance. This is a deliberate choice: an unbranded face becomes the brand's spokesperson, and the brand does not have one.
- No cosmetic "after" imagery, no skin close-ups implying a result. This is both a brand rule and a regulatory one (`02_brand_guidelines.md` §6).
- Where Mongolian herders appear, they are doing skilled work with correct equipment. Never posed as scenery, never anonymised into silhouette-as-decoration.
- Where a Thai consumer context appears (`/rituals/`, home lifestyle), the setting is a real, specific, contemporary interior — a Bangkok apartment kitchen at 7 a.m. — not a generic beige "wellness" set.

---

## 8. Post-production pipeline

Every generated still goes through the same steps before it enters `src/`.

1. Raw PNG lands in `asset-src/` (git-ignored). Never delete — re-crops must not require regeneration.
2. Crop to the slot's exact display ratio.
3. Resize to 2× the maximum rendered width.
4. Encode AVIF (quality ~50) and WebP (quality ~78) into `src/assets/<page>/`.
5. Verify the compressed file is under the §16 budget in `03_design_system.md` (< 220 KB).
6. Write the alt text from the placeholder block into the component. Do not leave it for later.

---

## 9. Review checklist per image

Before an image is accepted:

- [ ] Reads as a photograph, not a render
- [ ] Light has a single identifiable natural source
- [ ] At least two real materials are legible
- [ ] Contains at least one genuine imperfection
- [ ] Colour sits inside forest / cream / gold; nothing is oversaturated
- [ ] No text, logo, watermark or graphic baked in
- [ ] Negative space is where the slot needs it, and the intended text is legible over it at the smallest breakpoint
- [ ] If a pack is in frame, the label matches the real pack (see caveat below)
- [ ] No face to camera
- [ ] Sits beside the other images on its page without looking like a different shoot

> **Known caveat, carried from `STEPPE_GUT_HIGGSFIELD_PROMPTS.md`:** generated packaging invents its own label microcopy — sachet counts, net weights and category claims will not match the real pack. This is acceptable at card display sizes. **Any shot where label text is legible must be re-checked, and any shot on a product detail page must use the real pack cutout as `--image`.** Shipping an invented net weight on a PDP is a regulatory problem, not a cosmetic one.
